text: The lab results for your blood work, thyroid, and prolactin are all within normal limits, and your MRI brain scan shows no significant findings. Given your history of starting risperidone two months ago and the new onset of movement symptoms, do you notice any stiffness, tremors, or involuntary muscle movements in your face or limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms—specifically the inability to remain still, restlessness, and repetitive movements—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent initiation of risperidone, this is a likely side effect. Have you noticed any worsening of these symptoms after increasing your dose recently, or do you experience muscle pain or cramping?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of risperidone use and symptoms of inner restlessness with an urge to move, this is highly suggestive of drug-induced akathisia. Do you feel an intense need to pace or shift your weight to relieve the discomfort? Also, have you noticed any new muscle stiffness or tremors in your hands?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia. The combination of recent risperidone initiation and symptoms of inner restlessness, pacing, and an inability to remain still is classic for this adverse effect. I will recommend a reduction in the risperidone dose or switching to an atypical antipsychotic with a lower risk of extrapyramidal symptoms.
